activities.title: Logic gates
activities.description: Ten questions on AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND and NOR: truth tables, Boolean expressions, the half adder, and reading a logic circuit. Written for Leaving Certificate Computer Science.

config.title: Logic gates
config.instructions: Draw the truth table before you choose. Each question is worth 1 mark.

questions.stem: An AND gate has two inputs. For which combination of inputs is its output 1?
A two-input OR gate has inputs A = 0 and B = 1. What is its output?

options.text: It depends on a third input.
The output is undefined for mixed inputs.

questions.stem: Which statement describes an XOR gate with two inputs?

options.text: The output is 1 only when both inputs are 1.
The output is 1 when the two inputs are the same.
The output is always the opposite of input A.
The output is 1 when the two inputs are different.

questions.stem: A two-input NAND gate is given A = 1 and B = 1. What is its output?

options.text: The same as the inputs.
A NAND gate cannot take two 1s.

questions.stem: For which inputs does a two-input NOR gate output 1?

options.text: Only when both inputs are 1.
Only when both inputs are 0.
Whenever at least one input is 1.
Whenever the inputs are different.

questions.stem: Evaluate the Boolean expression when A = 1, B = 0 and C = 1.
questions.code: Q = (A AND NOT B) OR C

options.text: Q cannot be evaluated without a truth table.
Q = A

questions.stem: How many rows does the complete truth table of a circuit with 4 inputs have?
A half adder adds two single bits and produces a sum bit and a carry bit. Which pair of gates produces them?

options.text: Sum from an AND gate, carry from an XOR gate.
Sum from an OR gate, carry from a NOT gate.
Sum from an XOR gate, carry from an AND gate.
Both from a single NAND gate.

questions.stem: NAND is described as a universal gate. What does that mean?

options.text: It is the fastest gate to manufacture.
Every other logic gate can be built from NAND gates alone.
It accepts any number of inputs.
Its output is always 1.

questions.stem: A car should sound a warning buzzer when the engine is running AND a seatbelt is NOT fastened. The inputs are E (engine running) and S (seatbelt fastened). Which expression drives the buzzer?

options.text: E AND NOT S
E AND S
NOT E AND S
E OR NOT S

q1.explanation: AND outputs 1 only when every input is 1 — think of two switches in series, where the current gets through only if both are closed. All three other rows of the truth table give 0.

q2.explanation: OR outputs 1 when at least one input is 1, so 0 OR 1 = 1. Only 0 OR 0 gives 0. This is inclusive OR: unlike everyday English, 1 OR 1 is also 1.

q3.explanation: XOR — exclusive OR — outputs 1 exactly when the inputs differ, so 0⊕1 = 1⊕0 = 1 and 0⊕0 = 1⊕1 = 0. The answer that fires when the inputs are the same describes XNOR, the exact opposite.

q4.explanation: NAND is AND followed by NOT. 1 AND 1 = 1, and inverting that gives 0. In fact 1,1 is the only input pair for which a NAND gate outputs 0.

q5.explanation: NOR is OR followed by NOT. OR gives 1 for every combination except 0,0, so inverting it leaves NOR outputting 1 for 0,0 alone. Firing whenever at least one input is 1 describes plain OR, and firing whenever the inputs differ describes XOR.

q6.explanation: Work from the inside out: NOT B = NOT 0 = 1, so A AND NOT B = 1 AND 1 = 1. Then 1 OR C = 1 OR 1 = 1. Note the OR would have made Q = 1 on its own, because C = 1 — an OR gate needs only one 1.

q7.explanation: Each input doubles the number of combinations, so n inputs need 2^n rows: 2^4 = 16. Answering 4 confuses the number of inputs with the number of rows, and 8 is the answer for 3 inputs.

q8.explanation: In binary 1 + 1 = 10, so the sum bit is 0 and the carry is 1. XOR gives that sum column (1 only when the bits differ) and AND gives the carry (1 only when both bits are 1). A full adder chains two half adders to take a carry in as well.

q9.explanation: A NOT is a NAND with its inputs tied together, an AND is a NAND followed by that NOT, and OR follows from De Morgan's laws — so any circuit at all can be built from NAND alone. That matters industrially: one gate design can be etched over and over. NOR is universal for the same reason.

q10.explanation: Both conditions must hold at once, so it is an AND, and the seatbelt condition is the negative one, so S is inverted: E AND NOT S. E OR NOT S would sound the buzzer with the engine switched off, and E AND S would sound it when the belt is properly fastened.
